messages.subject: Error in eco.env.regression
parts:
Hello Will and fellow Pez users,

When using my data to run the eco.env.regression, I had the following error message:
"Error in pianka.dist.comparative.comm(data, altogether) : 
  Cannot calculate Pianka distances of environmental data non-factor-level environmental data"

After converting all of my environmental data to numeric, and still getting the same error, I ran the example data (laja), and it is still returning the same error. Any ideas?

Thanks in advance.

Tesa

messages.author: 67da97097034e6ca
messages.subject: Re: Error in eco.env.regression
parts:
Hello Tesa,

Thanks for this. I think the problem is a mis-reading of the error message: you can only calculate a Pianka distance if you've got factor-level data, and you don't have any factor-level data in your object. This has come up before: it's not really an error message, but rather this is how Pianka's distances work. Below is a quick example of what I'm talking about, and how to get going problem:

# Load pez
library(pez)

# Load data
data(laja)

# Make comparative.comm object
c.data <- comparative.comm(invert.tree, river.sites, env=river.env)

# Do work
model <- eco.env.regression(c.data)
#...snap, it doesn't work!

# Convert to factors (as a demo)
for(i in seq_len(ncol(river.env)))
    river.env[,i] <- factor(ifelse(river.env[,i] > median(river.env[,i]), "higher", "lower"))

# Now try it
c.data <- comparative.comm(invert.tree, river.sites, env=river.env)
model <- eco.env.regression(c.data)
#...hooray!

...the good news is that you don't have to use Pianka's distance if you don't want to - there are other options in pez. I'd take a look at the fingerprint.regression function (and the vignette, which has got an overview of the sorts of things you can do with it) if you're interested.

I hope that helps - if it doesn't, let me know!

Cheers,

Will
